Play. running shirt, and VIP access to pre-and post-race gear storage and recovery zones, all while supporting Oakland’s kids. Last year’s race weekend raised nearly $125,000 for Eat. Learn. articles.title: Luka Doncic's aggressive leadership gets JJ Redick's approval as Lakers coach pushes back against disrespect claims
articles.summary: JJ Redick has no problem with how Luka Doncic behaves during timeouts and at halftime.
articles.body: JJ Redick has no problem with how Luka Doncic behaves during timeouts and at halftime. The Lakers coach spoke to reporters Sunday after two clips involving Doncic went viral. In one, he takes a clipboard from assistant coach Lindsey Harding. In the other, the 6-foot-8 guard shouts profanities as the team heads to the tunnel against Sacramento. Some critics called both moments disrespectful toward the staff.Redick certainly has a different take. The Lakers beat the Kings 106-104 in the NBA Cup on Friday and are 14-3 overall, and he says the staff wants players to speak up in those moments. He also admitted he was angry himself that night. His explanation covers both clips.Redick says Doncic is leading, not ventingAsked about Luka Doncic's animated moments, Redick started with the clipboard clip and used it to explain how timeouts work with this group. The opening minute belongs to the players. Lately, the coach has been walking over early just to sit with them and say nothing.He credited Doncic with leading those conversations. "They are problem-solving in real time. We encourage that," Redick said. Players should say what they see before any coach adds to it. Neither Redick nor Harding took offense when the clipboard changed hands.The halftime clip drew a more personal answer. Redick called Doncic's approach good because he is leading rather than reacting out of frustration. Then he talked about his own mood. The Lakers were in a four-point game when they botched a two-for-one and then the final shot, and the gap grew to eight. Redick said he was steaming and may have raised his voice a little at halftime for the same reason.Why the Kings game got heated at halftimeSacramento arrived at 1-13, yet the first half still slipped away from Los Angeles. The Kings shot 52.1 percent and led 62-54 at the break. They made three shots in the final 45 seconds, and the last one came after a Sandro Mamukelashvili turnover with five seconds left, an easy layup for rookie Darius Acuff Jr.Baseline microphones and cameras picked up Doncic as he walked toward the tunnel, furious and shouting profanities toward the bench and staff. The Lakers still fixed things after the break. They held Sacramento to 42 second-half points on 38.1 percent shooting, and Doncic finished with 25 points and eight assists.Questions about his leadership have followed Doncic since Dallas traded him to Los Angeles. The Lakers also lean on him heavily on offense, and Austin Reaves has missed time with an injury, which adds to the load. Few stars carry that much of a team's scoring plan. Nikola Jokic is the closest comparison, and Denver has Jamal Murray sharing more of the work this season. Redick is in those huddles himself. His read is that the group is using that time well.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Will Bronny James meet Dalton Knecht's fate? Lakers' roster decision around LeBron James’ son raises fresh questions about his future
articles.summary: Bronny James is averaging 2.7 minutes per game in his third NBA season, one of the lowest marks on the Los Angeles Lakers roster.
articles.body: Bronny James is averaging 2.7 minutes per game in his third NBA season, one of the lowest marks on the Los Angeles Lakers roster. The team guaranteed his 2026-27 salary before the year began, so the 22-year-old guard has a spot for now, though that may not last.Dalton Knecht was not so lucky. The Lakers waived him in the preseason to get down to 15 players, and an insider has now named James as one of two players most likely to go if the team ever adds a veteran.Will Bronny James end up like Dalton Knecht with the Lakers?Bronny James and Dalton Knecht were both tied to trade talk this summer. Neither moved, and the Lakers had to cut a player to reach the league limit. Writer Tyler Watts says the choice came down to those two after James struggled through the preseason, and he sees a pattern forming. In his view, the situation "feels eerily similar to what happened to Dalton Knecht last season."“The Lakers waived Knecht in the preseason to get their roster down to 15 players. The battle was between him and Bronny after James struggled mightily during the preseason. L.A. wants Bronny to play point guard, but he keeps struggling in that role. It may already be too late for James,” Watts shared.Part of that is easy to see. James is playing only 2.7 minutes a night, and Watts says he mostly gets on the floor in blowouts. The Lakers want him at point guard, but he has not looked comfortable there. Head coach JJ Redick has not given him more time, even when the team's top guards were out.Rookie Cameron Carr has picked up G League minutes to build confidence. Watts says James has not. The roster is built to win around Luka Doncic, and Adou Thiero and Carr are also stuck with garbage time.How Bruce Brown could change the Lakers roster mathInsider Buha did not report any talks between the Lakers and Bruce Brown. He did explain what would have to give if a deal came together. His answer was Kevon Looney or James, since they are "the cheapest players on the roster." Buha also expects Los Angeles to keep Jaden Hardy and his $6 million salary as a trade chip.Brown was part of the Denver team that won the 2022-23 title. The Knicks signed him to an Exhibit 9 deal in September and let him go in October. Looney is a three-time champion with Golden State on a one-year minimum deal.There is no rush. The Lakers were 14-3 through Saturday, the best record in the West at that point. Austin Reaves missed the win over the Kings with a left heel bruise, and Redick expected him back for the Nov. 23 game against Utah or the Nov. 27 game against San Antonio. A healthy Reaves deepens the guard rotation, which leaves James more exposed than Looney if a veteran becomes a real option.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: LeBron James' wife Savannah sounds alarm over family safety as urgent court filing reveals growing concerns
articles.summary: Savannah James has asked a judge for temporary restraining orders against two men she says keep turning up uninvited at the family's Los Angeles
articles.body: Savannah James has asked a judge for temporary restraining orders against two men she says keep turning up uninvited at the family's Los Angeles properties. The separate requests name William Rahman, 55, and Jaliere McWhite, 22. She is seeking protection for herself, her husband LeBron James and their three children. No ruling has come yet, and hearings are set for Dec. 11. Officers responded to both situations, according to her. One filing says a man walked into a family home, and Savannah says relatives are now afraid to be inside it.What did Savannah James say about her family's safety?Savannah did not soften her language. "The James family faces imminent danger," she wrote. Another line in the filing says, "Family members are now afraid to be in their own home."The McWhite request starts on Oct. 23, when she says he appeared in the front driveway of a family residence, said he was related to the family, acted like a child and gave his age as 14. She called it a "delusional attachment to the family."Two weeks later, on Nov. 6, he climbed onto a neighboring property and entered through a front door relatives had left unlocked as they headed out. "Security footage confirms that he was inside the home," she wrote.Twelve LAPD officers came to order him out. "The seriousness of that response reflects how dangerous the situation was," Savannah said.McWhite was arrested over the Nov. 6 entry and is in custody, but Savannah wants an order in place in case he is released. "His history shows he will likely try to contact or approach the family again," her filing says.Rahman's visit and the hearing dateRahman's part of the story starts earlier. Savannah says he began sending mail and packages to her home in December 2025. They were rejected and returned, and her lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter on Feb. 23. By October, her security staff had spotted him loitering near the property with luggage.On Nov. 14, Rahman arrived by Uber with several bags and entered the driveway. Officers told him he was trespassing and could be arrested if he came back. He allegedly told them the property was his home and he would take legal action to have security removed.The request asks the court to keep him 200 yards from Savannah, LeBron and their children. It cites "a fixed, delusional belief that he lives at" the residence.LeBron, the 41-year-old 76ers forward, said days after McWhite's arrest the family was "looking into everything" and safe. He now plays in Philadelphia, while Savannah has stayed in Los Angeles.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: MVP SGA Reacts to Thunder Losing, Changing His Game amid Injuries to Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams
articles.summary: Oklahoma State Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is finding a silver lining with injuries to key players presenting a challenge to the team.
articles.body:
Oklahoma State Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is finding a silver lining with injuries to key players presenting a challenge to the team.

"We can't be at the top of the mountain every night for the next decade," he said, per ESPN's Tim MacMahon . "It doesn't work like that. It's motivation for me."

The Thunder have lost six of their last eight. Their slide coincides with Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace all being sidelined for significant stretches.

In the aftermath of the 113-112 defeat to the Los Angeles Clippers on Nov. 13, Gilgeous-Alexander asserted the difficult period is "kind of fun" in a way.

"We've kind of had the wind at our back for the last couple of years, had our way a lot of nights," he said. "Having adversity, it's kind of fun. I embrace it. It will make me better. It will make us better."

The two-time reigning MVP also reflected on how he has had to adapt. He was already a high-volume player, and now he needs to lead the show even more.

"I've always been at the top of the scouting report," Gilgeous-Alexander told MacMahon. "It's only amplified with guys out.

"Then [I'm] having to start games differently just because of the personnel out there. I've got to be more aggressive some nights to start the game. Typically, when we have our full roster, I'll get guys going and ease into the game. Some nights with men down, you can't really do that."

Some drew big-picture conclusions once the scale of the Thunder's injury crisis became clear. The NBA has made it harder to maintain a championship contender across multiple seasons, with OKC trading Luguentz Dort in the summer largely for financial considerations.

The title window hasn't closed, but a lost year is a bigger missed opportunity for the 2024-25 champion.

Maybe the Thunder's present situation will help them discover new things that aid in their quest for success once they're back to full strength.

articles.title: Donte DiVincenzo Injury Update, Latest NBA Rumors Reveal Timeline to Return for T-Wolves Guard
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves announced Tuesday that guard Donte DiVincenzo has been cleared for team activities as he works his way back from a torn Achilles.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves announced Tuesday that guard Donte DiVincenzo has been cleared for team activities as he works his way back from a torn Achilles.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported DiVincenzo is aiming to return around Jan. 1.

Minnesota is third in the Western Conference at 13-5 despite missing DiVincenzo and seeing Anthony Edwards go down with a knee injury in October.

Some questioned whether LaMelo Ball was the right star to target in a blockbuster trade. The move looks pretty shrewd now with how much he has had to anchor the backcourt. Ball is averaging 17.2 points and 5.6 assists.

Paying a premium to retain Ayo Dosunmu was also a sound investment. His 18.2 points per game are third on the team, and he's shooting 44.8 percent from beyond the arc.

Getting DiVincenzo back by early January would be a huge boost for the team.

The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski noted he's way ahead of schedule. Damian Lillard, Tyrese Haliburton, Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson all missed more than a calendar year. DiVincenzo might be suiting up 10 months removed from his Achilles tear.

The Wolves have no vague idea of when Edwards will be playing again, so they could be a ways off from competing at full strength. DiVincenzo's presence will at least alleviate the burden on Ball and Dosunmu a bit.

articles.title: Imparable crecimiento de la Euroliga: estrenará su propia Liga de Verano en 2027
articles.standfirst: Un torneo internacional con seis equipos y vocación de crecimiento. El proyecto refuerza su capacidad para generar iniciativas, abrir mercados y ampliar su influencia en el baloncesto
articles.summary: Un torneo internacional con seis equipos y vocación de crecimiento. El proyecto refuerza su capacidad para generar iniciativas, abrir mercados y ampliar su influencia en el baloncesto
articles.body: La Euroliga sigue ampliando sus horizontes. la máxima competición continental estrenará en 2027 su propia Liga de Verano, un nuevo proyecto con el que pretende crear un punto de encuentro internacional para jugadores, entrenadores y profesionales del baloncesto, según adelantó Eurohoops. Es una iniciativa que vuelve a poner de manifiesto la capacidad de la organización para impulsar nuevos formatos, detectar oportunidades y desarrollar propuestas que van más allá de la competición tradicional. Los planes de crecimiento de la Euroliga no se limitan a la ampliación de su estructura hasta los 24 equipos ni a la incorporación de nuevas franquicias. La organización presidida por su dirección ejecutiva, encabezada por Chus Bueno, trabaja también en la creación de nuevos espacios de desarrollo y negocio que permitan reforzar su posición dentro del panorama internacional del baloncesto. La primera edición de esta Liga de Verano podría contar con seis equipos y se disputaría durante aproximadamente diez días, incluyendo una semana de competición. Su celebración está prevista una vez concluidas las ligas nacionales y antes del tradicional torneo de verano de la NBA en Las Vegas. La ciudad que albergará el estreno todavía no está decidida, aunque se espera que el proyecto completo se presente en la próxima reunión de la Junta Directiva, prevista para el 30 de noviembre. La propuesta nace con una clara vocación internacional. El objetivo es reunir a jugadores y entrenadores procedentes de clubes de la Euroliga y la Eurocup, universidades estadounidenses y programas de baloncesto de África y Asia. Una combinación que permitiría generar nuevas oportunidades para el desarrollo de jugadores, facilitar la captación de talento y favorecer el intercambio de conocimientos entre distintas culturas baloncestísticas. La intención es que el torneo no sea un acontecimiento aislado, sino una plataforma anual que vaya ganando dimensión y relevancia con el paso de las temporadas. La Euroliga quiere comenzar con un formato reducido de seis participantes para después desarrollar progresivamente una competición capaz de hacerse un hueco propio en el calendario internacional. El proyecto supone, además, una nueva muestra de la ambición de una organización que lleva años diversificando sus iniciativas y explorando fórmulas para ampliar su influencia. La creación de competiciones, la expansión de su estructura y la búsqueda de nuevas vías de conexión con otros mercados forman parte de una estrategia que pretende consolidar a la Euroliga como algo más que una competición de clubes. No será la primera experiencia de la organización en este terreno. La Euroliga ya impulsó en el pasado, junto a Verde Sport, la Liga de Verano ULEB en Jesolo (Italia), aunque aquella iniciativa tuvo una duración de una sola temporada. Ahora, con un planteamiento más ambicioso y una clara vocación de continuidad, la Euroliga pretende recuperar aquella idea y convertirla en un proyecto de mayor alcance. El reto será transformar una competición de verano en una herramienta estable para conectar mercados, descubrir talento y generar nuevas oportunidades para el baloncesto europeo. Con este movimiento, la Euroliga vuelve a demostrar que su capacidad de crecimiento no depende únicamente de lo que sucede durante la temporada regular. También pasa por saber crear nuevos productos, gestionar proyectos de alcance internacional y anticiparse a las necesidades de una industria en constante evolución. La Liga de Verano de 2027 será el próximo desafío de una organización que quiere seguir ampliando su protagonismo en el baloncesto mundial.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Reveals WNBA Offseason Bucket List, Golf Goals in Video With Travis, Jason Kelce
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's offseason away from the WNBA will include a stop at one of the most legendary golf courses in the world.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark's offseason away from the WNBA will include a stop at one of the most legendary golf courses in the world.

The Indiana Fever star said last week on the New Heights podcast she's hopeful of attending Super Bowl LXI in Inglewood, California. She's also aiming to play a round at Augusta National Golf Club, adding she has "a couple of opportunities to do that" (30:30 mark).

Clark has golfed recreationally for most of her life. She said in a 2023 interview with Big Ten Network she started playing in elementary school.

Fans got to see the three-time All-Star in action at the Annika pro-am last fall.

Clark estimated her handicap is around 15, which is pretty solid for a full-time basketball player. She quipped to hosts Travis and Jason Kelce she benefits from starting off all the way up at the forward tees since she can get as much as 230 yards off her drives.

Augusta National has some of the most exclusive membership on the planet, and the course is closed to members for the best golfing months on the calendar.

Pretty much anybody who has picked up a set of clubs has dreamed about stepping onto the first tee at Augusta. Clark is one of the rare few who's presented with the chance.

articles.title: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation Eat, Learn & Play makes a new update as its Oakland partnership reaches another milestone in changing lives
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have achieved worldwide fame in the last decade but they have remained
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have achieved worldwide fame in the last decade but they have remained grounded to their roots. While they are multi millionaires, the two have continued to support the communities they have helped in their hometown, Oakland, for the last few years. Amid this, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation, Eat, Learn and Play has shared a new update.Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation Eat, Learn & Play makes a new update about their partnershipA few hours ago, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation Eat, Learn & Play made a post on social media as it read as, “Every kid deserves a safe, joyful place to play, move, and thrive. Since our first schoolyard build in 2021, @eatlearnplay has partnered with @kaboom, a national nonprofit working to end playspace inequity, to transform schoolyards across the Oakland Unified School District into spaces that support the whole child.”Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation Eat, Learn & Play added, “As KABOOM! celebrates 30 years of impact, their CEO @LysaRatliff joins us on our blog to share her thoughts on our partnership, why play matters, and what’s next. Read the conversation at the link in our bio.”In a press release, Lysa Ratliff, KABOOM! CEO reflected on their partnership with the NBA icon’s charity as she said, “KABOOM!’s partnership with Eat. Learn. Play. began in 2021 at Franklin Elementary, when we were focused on delivering each playground build as a single project. Franklin was one of our first living schoolyard builds; it was a larger and more innovative project than our traditional playgrounds, which included vibrant murals, multi-sport courts, and native plants and gardens that brought nature to kids who didn't live or learn near greenspaces.”Lysa Ratliff, KABOOM! CEO added, “We didn't know it then, but Franklin would become a model for how we'd continue to work in Oakland and a blueprint for what we hope to achieve nationwide. In 2022, as we launched our 25 in 5 Initiative to End Playspace Inequity, Eat. Learn. Play. and Oakland Unified School District (OUSD) were among our first initiative partners.”Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation has changed lives across OaklandStephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s foundation has been able to build 27 schoolyards at elementary schools across Oakland in the last few years while also providing quality education to children coming from disadvantaged families in Oakland.But that’s not all; the four time NBA champion has also been focused on providing quality meals to children and encouraging them to take up sports in their lives.While there might be a lot of scrutiny on their marriage, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry remain united in their efforts to helping children.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Hayes-Davis aparta del liderato al Valencia Basket con un triplazo sobre la bocina
articles.standfirst: El alero anota desde más de ocho metros para dar el triunfo al Panathinaikos y frustra el gran esfuerzo de los taronjas
articles.summary: El alero anota desde más de ocho metros para dar el triunfo al Panathinaikos y frustra el gran esfuerzo de los taronjas
articles.body: Un triplazo de Hayes-Davis sobre la bocina y desde más de ocho metros acabó con el líder Valencia Basket. Sólo así, con sucesos extraordinarios, cae este equipo. Los taronjas tuvieron al poderoso Panathinaikos a su merced (83-80 a 39 segundos del final), pero le rescataron la aparición de dos de sus estrellas. Primero Nunn, con un triple de siete metros, y luego el verdugo definitivo, con el tiro de gracia, dejaron dos destellos ganadores que apartaron a los valencianos de la primera plaza. Los dos equipos han cambiado mucho con respecto a la temporada pasada. Numerosas caras nuevas, pero la misma intensidad. El duelo de este martes recordó a la serie de playoffs del curso pasado, que también tuvo partidos resueltos sobre la bocina, incluido uno por Hayes-Davis. Fue una de las mejores que se recuerdan en la historia de la Euroliga. Este nuevo enfrentamiento no tuvo nada que envidiar a aquellos. La derrota es dolorosa para el Valencia, pero su consuelo es haber resistido a un transatlántico en un partido jugado a contrapelo en el que sólo en dos buenas rachas pudo imponer el baloncesto que le gusta. El resto del tiempo, el Panathinaikos le cambió el paso y le obligó a bajar al barro. En un gran trabajo defensivo destacaron Saint-Supéry, Cárdenas, Corbalán... Todos ellos se encargaron en algún momento de Nunn, al que contuvieron bien durante la primera mitad. Después, el talento se desbordó. Metió 13 puntos, pero en momentos clave. Shorts lideró un día más a los taronjas. Indefendible por momentos, es todo personalidad y carácter. Acabó con 15 puntos, siete asistencias y tres recuperaciones. Suya fue la canasta del 83-80. No pudo rematar Brooks, que fue de más a menos. Hizo 14 puntos y falló un triple crucial a falta de 10 segundos y con empate a 83. Hayes-Davis, sin embargo, no perdonó. El Valencia pudo ser él mismo en un tramo del primer cuarto para rehacerse de un flojo inicio. Brooks metió ocho puntos seguidos incluidos dos triples y Osetkowski metió otro para concretar un parcial de 11-0. Cárdenas y Corbalán le habían dado otro aire al equipo, pero Grant y la aparición de Yabusele mandaron en el segundo cuarto. El Panathinaikos no necesita ni puntería (1/9 en triples) para irse arriba al descanso: 34-39. Los griegos se fueron nueve arriba tras volver de los vestuarios (36-45). En el momento de mayor apuro se vio la mejor versión del Valencia, una en la que lució una defensa extraordinaria que le permitió volar. Tres minutos de baloncesto total para firmar un parcial de 13-0 con Shorts y Mirotic delante. Detrás mordían todos. Nunn se quitó los grilletes y, ayudado por el rebote ofensivo, el PAO devolvió el golpe con un 0-11 (57-64). En el último cuarto, apariciones de Rogkavopoulos y Juancho mantenían arriba a los visitantes, pero un par de robos del Valencia y el trabajo de Sako voltearon el asunto (75-74). El pívot fue de los destacados (13+7), pero volvió a flojear en el tiro libre (1/6) y arrastró a su equipo (10/19). Con el marcador convertido en un péndulo, Shorts lo puso del lado taronja. Dos de las estrellas de Obradovic acabaron decidiendo. 83.- Valencia Basket (19+15+25+24): TJ Shorts (15), Saint-Supéry (5), Taylor (5), Osetkowski (6), Sako (13) -cinco titular- Cárdenas (7), Moore (2), Corbalán (4), Puerto (-), Brooks (14), Gueye (4) y Mirotic (8). 86.- Panathinaikos (19+20+25+22): Francisco (4), Bonga (2), Hayes-Davis (11), Yabusele (10), Fall (6) -cinco titular- Badio (-), Rogkavapoulos (10), Grant (14), Nunn (13), Lessort (9) y Hernangómez (7). Árbitros: Belosevic (SER), Koljensic (MNE) y Sacys (LTU). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido correspondiente a la décimo cuarta jornada de la fase regular de la Euroliga disputado en el Roig Arena ante 14.130 espectadores.

articles.standfirst: El excelso alero resucita al Fenerbahce en su momento más bajo (59-47) liderando un parcial de 3-22 (62-69). Las cinco bajas azulgranas lastraron su encomiable resistencia
articles.summary: El excelso alero resucita al Fenerbahce en su momento más bajo (59-47) liderando un parcial de 3-22 (62-69). Las cinco bajas azulgranas lastraron su encomiable resistencia
articles.body: Shavon Shields anotó la primera canasta del Fenerbahce y luego desapareció, como si se le hubiera tragado la tierra. Tras un tobogán de parciales y contraparciales el mermado Barça pareció encarrilar el triunfo (59-47, min 27). Hasta que Shields resurgió como por arte de magia para comandar la remontada turca con 24 puntos más y 7/12 triples que arruinaron el esfuerzo de los azulgranas (77-83). El excelso alero entró en trance y en ocho minutos anotó cinco triples para liderar, con ayuda de Larkin y Juzang, un brutal parcial de 3-22 en apenas ocho minutos con el que el Fenerbahce dio la vuelta al marcador colocándose en una situación inmejorable que no desaprovechó. No se rindió el Barça, que con triples de Umude (69-71) y Martin (77-80) acarició la remontada. Pero Shields, con su séptimo triple y dos tiros libres abortó el conato de sorpasso y Horton-Tucker abrochase el triunfo turco con tres tiros libres y una canasta postrera. Fue la tercera derrota consecutiva de un Barça que reaccionó tras su flojo inicio (8-14) con un 20-7 (28-21, min 10) y un gran Minaya. El Fenerbahce contestó con un 2-13 con arreones de Larkin y Clyburn (30-34). Y Minaya, Martin y Umude llevaron a los azulgranas a su máxima (59-47) antes de la irrupción del ciclón Shields. Las bajas de Punter, Gibson, Nebo, Makoundou y Evbuomwoman pesaron más en el Barça que las de Melli y Key en el Fenerbahce de Jasikevicius, ídolo de un Palau que tuvo que rumiar su dolorosa derrota con Shavon Shields de ejecutor supremo.. 77 - Barça (28+17+16+16): Robinson (12), Brizuela (2), Minaya (13), Parra (4), Nkamhoua (3) -cinco inicial-, Martin (13), Umude (18), Ubal (1), Núñez (5) y Balcerowski (6). 83- Fenerbahce (21+18+14+30): Larkin (19), Shields (26), Clyburn (7), Horton Tucker (11), Powell (2) -cinco inicial-, Bingham (-), Baldwin IV (5), Sanli (3), Juzang (6) y Sariunas (4). Árbitros: Tomislav Hordov, Kristaps Kostantinovs y Luka Kardum. Eliminados: Sanli (min.33) y Powell (min.40). Incidencias: partido de la decimocuarta jornada de la Liga Endesa disputado en el Palau Blaugrana ante 5.698 espectadores.

articles.title: “Am I defective in some way?”: Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union on how she felt when she had to choose a surrogate to have her daughter
articles.summary: Dwyane Wade, the NBA icon, and his wife, the popular actress Gabrielle Union, have always been public about the issues they have faced in their marriage.
articles.body: Dwyane Wade, the NBA icon, and his wife, the popular actress Gabrielle Union, have always been public about the issues they have faced in their marriage. While they remain happily married with a daughter, life was not always so easy for them and especially for Gabrielle Union.Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union shared how tough it was for her to accept that she won't be able to carry a childA few years ago, the NBA legend Dwyane Wade and his wife, Gabrielle Union, made an appearance for an interview with Oprah Winfrey as she reflected on her fertility issues.The popular actress Gabrielle Union said, "you work hard, you do the right things, you're a good person…I could not let go of this idea of creating this life within me. I need to be pregnant for everybody, including myself."Dwyane Wade’s wife Gabrielle Union added, "Did I miss—did I fail in some kind of way? Did I—am I defective in some kind of deep, you know, just—am I defective in some kind of way? Am I less than in some kind of way? Am I less worthy in some kind of way?"To this, the Miami Heats’ legend Dwyane Wade added how he tried to help his wife, Gabrielle Union, As he said, "I'm watching her do things to her body and to herself that it's getting to the point where it's not healthy…And as I always told her: 'I want this baby just as much as you do, but I married you, and you are the most important thing to me.'”Dwyane Wade continued, “So it came to a point where, you know, I started to feel a certain way about that because I didn't want something to happen to her.'"In the end, Dwyane Wade and his wife, Gabrielle Union, chose surrogacy to bring their daughter into the world.Gabrielle Union has shared how difficult it was for her as Dwyane Wade stands by her sideIn many of her appearances, the actress Gabrielle Union has shared how tough it was for her to hold their daughter for the first time when she was born as she kept comparing how she was not able to carry a child as compared to her surrogate.For the unversed, the star actress has experienced over 8 miscarriages as she tried her best to carry her child to full term.The experience devastated her as she faced a pretty challenging time in accepting that she will never be able to give birth to a child on her own.Since then, she has become more and more public about her health issues as she has even spoken about her menopause issues.Today, Dwyane Wade and Gabrielle Union are parents to an 8 year old daughter as they remain private about their lives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Real Madrid busca una salida a su laberinto
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, que este miércoles reciben al Zalgiris, acumulan más pérdidas (51) que asistencias (48) en los últimos tres partidos
articles.summary: Los blancos, que este miércoles reciben al Zalgiris, acumulan más pérdidas (51) que asistencias (48) en los últimos tres partidos
articles.body: Las estadísticas no lo muestran todo ni son una verdad absoluta, pero en ocasiones sí se corresponden con la realidad. En el caso del Real Madrid hay algunas cifras que muestran el bajón que ha dado en cuestión de una semana. El juego fluido se esfumó en los tres últimos encuentros ante el Besiktas, el Olympiacos y el Asisa Joventut, saldados con dos derrotas y un triunfo sufrido. Entre esas citas, los madridistas acumularon más pérdidas (51) que asistencias (48), un registro significativo. En lo que iba de temporada promediaban 14,0 y 21,6, respectivamente, y esa estadística adversa sólo la habían sufrido en una ocasión, frente al UCAM Murcia. "No hemos jugado como nos gustaría y estamos más preocupados. Estamos en dificultades y debemos afrontarlas mirándolas a la cara", reconocía Pedro Martínez en la previa ante el Zalgiris Kaunas. Pese a todo, el técnico se muestra satisfecho con el trabajo de los suyos. "Estoy muy contento. Y lo digo en una semana que no hemos jugado bien y que no hemos tenido buenos resultados. El equipo lo está intentando, está trabajando con buena mentalidad", asegura el técnico, que sigue esperando a los lesionados. Facundo Campazzo podría volver la próxima semana, pero a Mikael Jantunen, Gabriel Deck y sobre todo a Usman Garuba aún les queda. "Se nos está haciendo un poco largo no recuperar a jugadores que están llamados a ser muy importantes", dice. Mientras eso sucede, el entrenador madridista pide "intentar competir, apretar los dientes y mejorar en lo que dependa de nosotros para ser competitivos, porque ahora mismo estamos un poco en un modo supervivencia". Martínez sí ha visto que "la impotencia nos ha podido, al ver que las cosas no nos salen como nos gustaría, nos hemos desmoralizado un poco por no poder competir como nos gustaría o como hemos hecho durante bastantes partidos". Tras las dos derrotas consecutivas en la Euroliga a domicilio, el Madrid vuelve al Movistar Arena, donde sólo el Panathinaikos consiguió ganar en el último año. El Zalgiris, que le aventaja en una victoria en la clasificación (8-5), será una buena prueba para comprobar la capacidad blanca para superar situaciones adversas. Los lituanos llegan con el exNBA Jonas Valanciunas como estandarte. La mole (2,11 metros y 120 kilos) está promediando 12,5 puntos y es el máximo reboteador de la Euroliga con 8,8 capturas por partido. Carsen Edwards pone la amenaza exterior (16,5 puntos con 6,6 triples lanzados por partido) y el polivalente Azuolas Tubelis sigue confirmándose como uno de los jugadores de mayor progresión (12,5 puntos y 6,0 rebotes).

articles.title: Pistons' Cade Cunningham to miss Tuesday's NBA Cup matchup vs. Magic due to right knee soreness
articles.summary: Cunningham was scratched from the lineup after being listed as probable up until a half-hour before tip-off.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham is out for Tuesday's NBA Cup matchup with the Orlando Magic . He was a late scratch due to right knee soreness after being listed as probable on the injury report until a half-hour before tip-off.

Cunningham, 25, has missed only one game this season for the Pistons, sitting out last week's 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans , also due to right knee soreness. Javonte Green replaced Cunningham in Detroit's starting lineup for that contest, scoring 18 points with seven rebounds.

"He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff told reporters Tuesday , via MLive's Jacob Richman. "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got, but he's fighting through a lot."

Cunningham scored a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks, shooting 2-for-9 in 33 minutes. His 15 assists were his highest total this season, but he also committed six turnovers.

The Pistons have lost two straight games and have a 10-6 record that has them tied for fifth in the Eastern Conference .

In his 15 games this season, Cunningham leads the Pistons in scoring with 24.2 points per game, while averaging 8.3 assists, 5.1 rebounds and 1.3 steals. He's shooting 32% on 92 3-point attempts.

Detroit will also be without Duncan Robinson (left quad strain) and Jalen Duren (strained right hamstring) against the Magic. However, Duren appears to be on his way back after being assigned to the Pistons' G League affiliate for Wednesday's practice.

The Pistons next play on Friday versus the Milwaukee Bucks.

articles.title: 5-Star Guard Jalen Davis Reveals CBB Commitment Decision Between Gonzaga, UNC More
articles.summary: Jalen Davis is staying close to home.
articles.body:
The 5-star guard from Washington announced on Tuesday that he would commit to Gonzaga, giving the Bulldogs the top-ranked recruit in the state.

He chose Gonzaga over North Carolina, UCLA and Washington.

Ranking Top 9 Players to Watch in MCBB 👀

"Coach Few is incredibly competitive and knows the game inside and out," Davis said, per ESPN's Jeff Borzello and Paul Biancardi . "I believe in his vision for me. I want to win and make the right reads. I watch film of Ryan Nembhard and Jalen Suggs because their games are similar to mine."

The 6-foot-4 guard out of Bremerton High School in Washington is ranked as the No. 29 prospect in ESPN's Next 100 and is their sixth-ranked shooting guard.

Davis led the Adidas 3SSB AAU circuit in scoring and steals last summer for the Slow Grind Elite squad, where he averaged 24.3 points and 2.8 steals over 12 games.

North Carolina heavily pursued Davis, but he had long been expected to stay out west. A versatile guard who can be a playmaker as a point guard or create his own offense at the two, the two-time Washington state high school champion made his announcement at his high school on Tuesday afternoon.

"I trusted my gut," Davis told ESPN. "From the moment I visited Gonzaga, it felt like home. The Kennel has a great atmosphere. Those are the people I want to surround myself with, both on and off the court."

Before narrowing down his list, Davis had also considered Stanford, Texas Tech, BYU, Iowa, Ole Miss, TCU and USC.

Davis is Gonzaga's second commit for 2027 along with Dooney Johnson, another top-ranked shooting guard prospect, giving Bulldogs coach Mark Few his first multiple top-30 signings since 2021, according to ESPN, when he signed Chet Holmgren and Hunter Sallis. Davis is the highest-ranked prospect to join the program since that recruiting class.

The Bulldogs are 3-1 and ranked No. 22 in the country so far this season.

articles.title: Thanks to sustained health, Daniel Gafford has been man in middle Mavs have been missing
articles.summary: After an injury-riddled 2025-26, Gafford has been a consistent presence for Dallas so far this season.
articles.body:
DENVER – The NBA Cup is in its fourth year of existence, but the tournament's prize money is one of the primary incentives to compete if you ask Daniel Gafford.

"A lot of guys are coming out and they're playing their tails off because who doesn't want a good stack of cash?" Gafford said after Tuesday's shootaround at Ball Arena. "From a team perspective, we lock in and it's just another game on our schedule. We want to win games. We want to stack these wins."

The Dallas Mavericks entered their pivotal NBA Cup matchup against the Denver Nuggets in the midst of their third three-game win streak of the season, hoping to use the lessons they learned from earlier in the season to extend it to four. Their attention to detail has been a key difference, but they're also getting healthier by the day.

Gafford's sustained health has contributed to those victories. For the Mavericks, that means they have a reliable starter at the center position who has regained his status as one of the most efficient scorers at the rim and shot blockers in the NBA.

The eighth-year big man has played in every game this season, averaging 8.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.6 blocks per game. He ranks eighth in the league in blocks per game, which is a key reason why the Mavericks are 12th in the NBA in defensive rating.

Gafford said he feels good holding down the paint while they await reinforcements from Dereck Lively II, who remains sidelined to rehabilitate from his right foot surgery .

"I'm a junkyard dog, man. I'm from Arkansas," Gafford said. "It ain't really too much that can hold me down."

Last season, Gafford missed 27 games to injury, mainly because of a lingering right ankle sprain. Despite suffering a right shoulder stinger in last Saturday's loss to Cleveland , he's been consistent and has scored in double figures in seven games this season. He's also added the occasional 3-pointer to his arsenal, with a perfect mark from distance on his two attempts.

"When bigs start making them, they change their game," said Mavericks coach Dusty May. "He's changing his game but it's to be an enforcer down low."

When the Mavericks are healthy, they have two big men who could start between Gafford and Lively, who spent a portion of shootaround sprinting, jogging and working on drills that included light jumps.

Gafford's primary backup center has been rookie Morez Johnson Jr., the No. 9 overall pick. Both players go through their pregame routines at the same time, lending itself to a natural partnership. Johnson is averaging 6.3 points and 4.7 rebounds and has connected on a 3-pointer in each of his last two games. The veteran big man said Johnson has developed well despite a slow start due to shin injuries.

"He's asserting himself in his role," Gafford said. "He's rebounding a lot. He's an energy guy. He's one of the strongest guys on our team, too. It's hard for a lot of people to move him. He's going to get into a lot of people's heads when it comes to setting screens and going for rebounds."

As for Gafford, he remains one of the best screen setters on the team and he's third in rebounding behind P.J. Washington and Cooper Flagg.

For the Mavericks to remain above .500, they'll need Gafford to continue to stay healthy and efficient on both sides of the floor.

articles.title: Analysis: No. 19 BYU melts down late in Maui, struggling mightily against elite Ole Miss defense
articles.summary: Leading by 14 points at halftime, the Cougars committed 15 second-half turnovers against five made field goals.
articles.body:
LAHAINA, Hawaii — Less than 24 hours after opening its Maui Invitational stay with a second-half comeback victory, BYU found itself as the team collapsing after halftime.

Having led Ole Miss by 14 after 20 minutes, the Cougars allowed the rabid Rebels to explode for 17 unanswered points out of intermission and never recovered, ultimately falling 73-63 for their first loss of the campaign.

There would have been no shame for BYU in losing to Ole Miss — the best opponent it's faced thus far in the season — and doing so on little rest and with star point guard Rob Wright III sidelined.

But to have led the Rebels by as many as 18 points, only to end up losing by 10? To play their best half of the season and follow it with their worst?

It was a brutal, disheartening outcome for the Cougars, and one that will be tough to flush ahead of Wednesday's final Maui contest.

"Tale of two halves, obviously," Kevin Young told reporters postgame. "We came out of the gate with great intensity, great ball security, great defense. And then, obviously, at the end of the first half and into the second, they obviously took the game over.

"So you've got to give Ole Miss all the credit. They played really good, they clearly accepted whatever coach (Chris) Beard said to them at halftime. We've got to be better, bottom line. In these types of environments, you've got to have a short memory, so we're trying to move on to the next game."

BYU was unfazed early against the vaunted, disruptive Ole Miss defense, scoring 40 points before halftime at an average of 1.2 points per possession. The Cougars appeared confident, comfortable and were seemingly cruising to Wednesday's Maui title game, only for the cruise to sink in spectacular, Titanic fashion.

Ole Miss' 17-0 run out of halftime soon ballooned to a 32-10 stretch. Through the first 15 minutes of the second half, BYU managed just two made field goals, while the Rebels generated turnovers left and right and cashed them in for easy transition buckets.

When Ole Miss turned up the heat in the second half, the Cougars slipped in their own sweat. Much of the guts and grit BYU displayed against Washington on Monday were absent in Tuesday's crunch time.

"We knew they were going to come out (of halftime ready to play). We said in the locker room, 'They're over there, going 'rah rah,' trying to get going,' and we came out and looked like we didn't expect that to happen, but it did," Young said of BYU's second-half struggles.

"I think it was a tough learning moment for us as a team, in getting a lead, keeping a lead and setting the tone in the second half."

In the final 20 minutes, BYU shot just 5 of 20 (25%) from the field and coughed up 15 turnovers, including five from Bruce Branch III alone.

If not for 17 free-throw attempts (10 coming from Collin Chandler), BYU would have barely had any sort of second-half offense. The Cougars were in constant distress, as evidenced by their turnover tally being three times that of their made field goals.

"In the first half we made it easy because we were the ones that came out and set the tone, we were getting turnovers and getting out in transition," Chandler said.

"They're a great set defense team, and they force turnovers that way. I think they're the best in the country at doing that ... We're a very experienced team, but that was a little bit of an inexperienced look for us, thinking they weren't going to come out and do that in second half. They completely flipped the script."

Chandler was sensational for the Cougars, pouring in a career-high 34 points on 9 of 18 shooting while adding eight rebounds and a pair of steals. The junior guard also went 12 of 13 from the foul line, which proved to be BYU's only source of consistent offense after halftime, as previously mentioned.

"We're in a little bit of a tough spot without Rob Wright, honestly, so that puts a little bit more responsibility on me to get downhill," Chandler said. "I think I learned a lot today. There's a lot that I can grow from in mistakes that I made, and so today was a good opportunity for me to learn especially and move on to tomorrow and get better at those things that Ole Miss exposed."

Unfortunately for Chandler, his 34 points were joined by just 29 from the rest of his teammates, who were stripped for 19 turnovers as well.

Aside from Chandler's three made triples, BYU netted just a single 3-pointer in 22 attempts.

"I thought Collin was amazing. We put the ball in his hands a lot, (and he) put a lot of pressure on them. Again, Ole Miss deserves all the credit, they made the plays, but it felt like we were not playing intelligent," Young said.

"... It was just frustrating because we felt like it was self-inflicted wounds ... for me, the biggest takeaway is just having better offensive integrity coming into a game where we know a team's going to be super aggressive (defensively)."

With Tuesday's performance, Ole Miss is KenPom's No. 1-rated defensive unit, boasting an adjusted efficiency mark of 89.6 — more than a point better than No. 2 Houston.

As for BYU's perimeter operation, the Cougars are now 11 for 51 (22%) from 3-point range in Maui, after having shot 42% from deep back in Utah.

So much for those famous "soft rims" at the Lahaina Civic Center.

"I thought this was a game where we would get a lot of open looks. If you look at the starters, by way of example, I mean, Collin goes 3 of 6, and then you've got Jax (Kohler) Bruce, Tyler (Betsey), Jake (Wahlin), that lineup went 0 for 18. It's going to be tough to win games when that happens," Young said.

"We have a lot of good shooting. All of our guys know that they can make shots, and I look forward to seeing more of that tomorrow, where they're actually going in."

With the loss, BYU is now 6-1 on the season and eliminated from Maui Invitational championship contention, as the 1992-93 Cougars will remain the only team in school history to reach the event's title game.

BYU will face either Arizona or Providence in Wednesday's third-place game at 3:30 p.m. MST.

"You just flush (today) and you move on. We've got to worry about what type of binds whoever we are going to play is going to put us in," Young said.

"Then, once we get home from this tournament, then you kind of do a deep dive on what you learned from the tournament as a whole."

articles.title: Does it matter how star-studded Sixers are winning and losing games?
articles.summary: One has to wonder if it matters how the star-studded Philadelphia 76ers are winning and losing games.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers are sitting at 14-4 and atop the Eastern Conference despite Monday's 128-111 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers at home. The Sixers are 12-0 in clutch games (games categorized as a 5-point spread or less with five minutes left in the game) and they have been terrific in terms of closing games out, but one has to wonder if it matters how the Sixers are winning and losing games.

Of their 14 wins, four of them have been by double-figures, and all four of their losses have been by double-figures. Therefore, one can summarize that the Sixers are winning close games, but losing in a tough fashion in those instances.

By true logic, a win is a win, and that's all that matters in the grand scheme of things, but to some, it does matter how the Sixers are winning.

"Yes. It matters because we want to build habits," said LeBron James after the win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 21. "We want to try to take steps forward every game that we get the opportunity to do. I know sometimes that it doesn't happen that way, but we want to do that. We want to strive to be as great as we can every night, offensively, defensively, special teams. So, yeah, I mean, a win is a win, but there is ways to win, and there's ways to continue to build habits throughout the course of this marathon."

Building wining habits is the name of the game right now. The Sixers can lean on their talent of James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, and others, but that won't matter unless they have the correct habits. Philadelphia has gotten off to a good start as it has begun to rely on each other and trust each other, but there is work to be done.

"I think we've bought into the pass," James explained. "We have so many guys that can score the ball at elite levels, and we know how we all, myself, VJ, JB, Max, Anfernee (Simons). You know, we have guys that can beat guys off the bounce. We know we have that in our ability. But in order for us to be like a super complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious, and it also just, it's key for our other guys as well to make sure to they feel like in a rhythm and they feel confident."

There were times it felt like the Sixers were doing a bit too much in terms of trying to get everybody going with the passing, but James sees improvements. There are still areas Philadelphia needs to get better in, like the defensive end of the floor as there has been slippage in recent games, but the Sixers are in a good spot.

"I think early on, like preseason, it looked a little weird," James continued. "Guys were like overpassing, you know, looking weird. But that's been great. And I think for the majority, our defense has been really good for the majority of the season. Tonight wasn't so great, but we've been really good defensively throughout the course of the season. Actually, better than our offense if you look at the numbers and things like that. So I don't want to say anything bad. There's so many things for us to do better, for sure."

So, does it matter how the Sixers win and lose games? Maybe so, but Philadelphia is succeeding in a lot of areas and it is winning basketball games. There is still work to be done, but the goal isn't to peak in November. The goal is to peak in April and May.

"There's games where we can defensive rebound a lot better," James finished. "There's games we can not turn the ball over. There's games where we can be a little bit more physically, physical defensively at the point of attack, like tonight. Wouldn't say anything has been bad, though, and that's a good thing. We want to continue to have room for improvement, and we don't want to be great in November either. That will be weird."

articles.title: What Ole Miss basketball’s Chris Beard said about Rebels’ insane comeback win over BYU
articles.summary: As the Ole Miss basketball team added another win to their season to put them at 6-0, it wasn’t just any ordinary victory, with the program getting a 73-63 r...
articles.body:
As the Ole Miss basketball team added another win to their season to put them at 6-0, it wasn't just any ordinary victory, with the program getting a 73-63 result against the No. 19 BYU Cougars. With the Ole Miss basketball team led by head coach Chris Beard , he would give his thoughts on the win, but more importantly, how the Rebels executed a marvelous comeback.

In the Southwest Maui Invitational game on Tuesday, the unranked Rebels were down to the Cougars at halftime, 40-26, but a spark was made in the second half by Ole Miss. With the Rebels outscoring the Cougars in the second half, 47-23, Beard was asked by Andy Katz what went into the halftime adjustments, giving insight into what the locker room was like.

"We have a veteran team," Beard said. "These guys have worked really hard since the first day of the summer. We've had some adversity along the way. This was our first adversity in the regular season, but it was really a calm halftime, and just asking the guys like, 'Hey, man, we're in the Maui Invitational. Are we going to compete this half?' Then once we decided we were going to play a little bit harder, then we got back to the original game plan."

The Ole Miss basketball team has been on a roll this season, but the win over BYU could give them national attention, especially when it comes to the rankings. Beard said that the comeback win over the Cougars is one that he will "remember."

"A tale of both halves," Beard continued. "Give BYU a lot of credit playing under man without their playmakers, but give our guys a lot of credit too. We're here. We came to Maui to win three games. Most people maybe didn't think that was probable, but we have an opportunity tomorrow to do that."

At any rate, Beard and the Rebels look to keep it going with their next game on Wednesday afternoon in the invitational, though the opponent has yet to be determined.

articles.title: Lakers are 15-3, but here’s why 1 ESPN insider is hating on NBA title contender status
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are having a blast to start the 2026-27 NBA season, but not everyone is completely sold just yet on the team’s status as an NBA champi...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are having a blast to start the 2026-27 NBA season, but not everyone is completely sold just yet on the team's status as an NBA championship contender.

Luka Doncic and the Lakers have a 15-3 record entering Tuesday, tied for the best record (but technically second) with the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference standings. They have also lost just once over their last 10 outings. For Tim MacMahon of ESPN, however, that record is not enough to label the Lakers as a legitimate NBA title contender, simply because he has yet to see the team take on some of the better teams in the league.

"I think the biggest overreaction is that the Lakers are clearly championship contenders," MacMahon said on Get Up YouTube Exclusive. "I'm not saying they can't be. I'm just saying they haven't proven to be with this great start that they've had against the No. 29 schedule in terms of opponents' winning percentage."

But MacMahon and other Lakers doubters can find out more about LA's true strength when the team hits th road for an upcoming road trip. That includes an upcoming Lakers-Spurs showdown on Friday.

"Now we're gonna learn a lot more about the Lakers over these next few games," MacMahon continued. "They've got a road trip at San Antonio, at Memphis, at Houston. You know, if they come out of that road trip looking rosy, then maybe it's time to reconsider. But I think it's premature to put the Lakers in the conversation with the best teams in the league."

articles.title: New NBA Rumors Reveal Clippers Stance on Trade Market Amid Brook Lopez, Max Strus, Kris Dunn Buzz
articles.summary: As rumors heat up around the Los Angeles Clippers, there is some more clarity about what they might do.
articles.body:
As rumors heat up around the Los Angeles Clippers, there is some more clarity about what they might do.

NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that the Clippers are "quietly insisting" that they are not yet ready to field the expected offers.

General manager Trent Redden has "full authority" to make any move he wants, according to Fischer, though several front office executives in the NBA, there is skepticism of if the Clippers can actually make a "significant deal" with owner Steve Ballmer and president Lawrence Frank suspended.

The Clippers have several expiring contracts, such as Brook Lopez, Kris Dunn and Max Strus, who are expected to be heavily pursued on the trade market.

But according to Fischer, the Clippers want to see what they have as Brandon Ingram gets integrated into the lineup. He made his season debut on Monday against Houston after undergoing offseason heel surgery and was the key piece in the Clippers' trade of Kawhi Leonard to Toronto.

Yet the Clippers have been showcasing their veteran players, which could make them more tantalizing if and when the time comes to make the trade.

Fischer reported that teams have already made calls for Lopez and Derrick Jones Jr., who each have contracts that should make it easy to bring them into most teams' salary cap situations.

Fischer's sources say that there is "no imminent trade" involving any of the Clippers' veteran players, but leading into the February 11 trade deadline, there is sure to be more discussion around all of them.

The Clippers have struggled to start the season, now at 4-12 since trading Leonard in September. They've lost their last four games after several late-game collapses, as Darius Garland has struggled from the field, and they have still yet to win a game on the road.

articles.title: New Anthony Davis Trade Rumors on Updated Landing Spots, Wizards' Stance Amid Warriors, Hawks Buzz

articles.body:
There could be several suitors for Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis on the trade market if the team makes him available.

The Golden State Warriors, Atlanta Hawks and Toronto Raptors have been mentioned as teams to watch regarding Davis, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer .

That doesn't necessarily mean the 10-time All-Star will experience a change of scenery prior to this season's deadline, though.

"My sense is that the Wizards have no imminent designs on moving Davis," Fischer reported Tuesday. "Could that change between now and the Feb. 11 trade buzzer? Conceivably. But I'm also told that Davis — unlike New Orleans' Dejounte Murray — is not pushing for relocation. Both players are represented by Klutch Sports, but it's been conveyed to me that there are no current plans for Davis to request a trade."

The 33-year-old is beginning his first full season in Washington after it acquired him from the Dallas Mavericks as part of a three-team trade on Feb. 5.

Davis and the Wizards chose to hold off on contract extension negotiations during the 2026 offseason, but the lack of an agreement could lead to opposing front offices inquiring about his availability.

He's earning $58.5 million this season before he holds a $62.8 million player option for his 2027-28 campaign (via Spotrac ).

David Aldridge and Josh Robbins of The Athletic previously reported that teams around the NBA are "well" aware that Davis' camp is searching for a contract that will "pay him at, or very near, maximum salaries."

Given the uncertainty surrounding his long-term future in Washington, as well as the fact that he doesn't fit the exact timeline of a Wizards squad looking to build around standout rookie AJ Dybantsa moving forward, he's been involved in plenty of trade rumors this year.

Davis has thrived to begin this season, as he entered Tuesday's action averaging 25.1 points, 9.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.1 blocks per game while shooting 53.3 percent from the field.

He owns the second-highest net rating among all Wizards players to appear in at least 10 games this season (via NBA.com ).

The Boston Celtics remain undefeated in the NBA Cup.

It was quite the roller-coaster ride, however, as Boston nearly blew a massive lead en route to a 131-116 win over the Washington Wizards in East Group C play.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

It was yet another impressive shooting display from Jayson Tatum, Paul George and the rest of the Celtics, who finished 22-of-51 (43 percent) from three on the night and dished out 30 assists.

But it didn't come easy. The Celtics led by as many as 34 points and were up 31 at halftime, though the Wizards cut that deficit down to five late in the fourth quarter.

But the Celtics held on for dear life and secured the victory. That left them very much in the driver's seat in Group C, moving to 3-0 in NBA Cup group stage play. Washington, meanwhile, could be eliminated by one of several scenarios playing out going forward after moving to 2-2 in Group C.

It was a double whammy loss for the Wizards (7-12), ending their much-needed three-game winning streak after the team suffered through an eight-game losing streak.

The Celtics (12-6) desperately needed the dub, meanwhile, ending a four-game skid of their own.

articles.title: Tessa Johnson scores career-high 32 points to lead No. 1 South Carolina to win over No. 7 UConn
articles.summary: The Gamecocks improved to 7-0 to begin the 2026-27 season, grinding out a win over the Huskies at Mohegan Sun Arena.
articles.body:
No. 1 South Carolina improved its record to 7-0 with a 65-56 win over No. 7 UConn in a clash of top 10 teams at the Hall of Fame Women's Showcase on a less-than-neutral court at Mohegan Sun Arena in Connecticut on Tuesday.

There was no pregame drama or apparent tension between the two head coaches. UConn's Geno Auriemma and South Carolina's Dawn Staley shook hands without incident following last season's postgame confrontation when the Gamecocks defeated the Huskies in the Final Four .

Tessa Johnson tallied a career-high 32 points for the Gamecocks in what was an offensive struggle for both teams. The senior guard shot 10-of-24 from the floor, but swished nine of 10 free throws and was South Carolina's only consistent scoring threat.

UConn was led by 22 points and 12 rebounds from Sarah Strong. However, in what's been a recurring issue for the Huskies star, she was limited by foul trouble. With four personal fouls at the end of the third quarter, Strong sat out for the opening three minutes of the fourth and added 7 points to her total.

Popovic and Vukosa each finished with 9 points for the Huskies, who shot 27% (17-of-64) overall.

The Huskies cut South Carolina's lead to single digits at 54-46 on two Olivia Vukosa foul shots with just over four minutes remaining in regulation. But Johnson responded with two baskets to knock UConn back against the ropes.

The Huskies went ahead 7-0 early on with Jovana Popovic scoring 5 of those points, South Carolina finally got on the board four minutes into the game on a 3-pointer from Jordan Lee. UConn increased its lead to 11-3 before the Gamecocks scored 8 points through the remainder of the quarter.

South Carolina shot 19% (3-for-16) in the opening 10 minutes, including 1-for-7 from behind the arc. The Gamecocks finished at 32% (20-for-63) from the floor, but eventually went 33% (8-of-24) on 3-pointers.

The Gamecocks eventually took a 22-20 lead with five minutes before halftime on a 3 by Lee. They extended the margin to 27-22 with Ashlyn Watkins scoring two baskets off turnovers. Tessa Johnson hit 3-pointers on consecutive possessions to put South Carolina ahead by 12 points.

A 16-0 run for the Gamecocks ended with a 4-point play by Agot Makeer to push their lead to 38-22 going into the fourth quarter.

South Carolina won without leading scorer Joyce Edwards

The Gamecocks played without junior forward Joyce Edwards, announcing that she would be out of the lineup due to illness approximately an hour before tipoff.

Edwards is South Carolina's leading scorer at 18 points per game, while also averaging 6.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.8 steals. She had started the Gamecocks' past 46 games.

UConn was also missing one of its best players on Tuesday. Senior guard KK Arnold was a late scratch after sustaining a lower-body injury during shootaround, the team announced.

Arnold is the Huskies' fourth-leading scorer at 8.2 points per game and is shooting 42% on 12 3-point attempts.

UConn drops to 4-3 after last season's 38-1 record and has lost two of its past three games. The Huskies scored fewer than 60 points in both defeats. Up next for Auriemma's squad is a matchup with No. 5 Duke at TD Garden in Boston on Saturday.

South Carolina follows up Tuesday's win by facing Tennessee State at home before visiting Cameron Indoor Stadium on Dec. 3 to presumably extend its undefeated start to the season.

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026: Celtics avert disaster, Mavs roll listless Nuggets, Pistons deny Magic without Cade Cunningham
articles.summary: Cooper Flagg and the Mavericks silenced the Nuggets in Denver to take control of their group.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics entered halftime of Tuesday's NBA Cup game apparently well on their way to snapping a four-game losing streak .

They eventually got there. But it wasn't easy as they had to fend off a furious comeback effort from the Washington Wizards.

The Celtics opened an 80-49 lead at halftime that the Wizards cut to 117-112 in the final four minutes. But the Celtics held on from there to avert disaster via a 131-116 victory.

A Jayson Tatum 3 and two more by Baylor Scheierman in the game's final minutes helped ensure that the Celtics got back into the win column.

With the win, the Celtics improved to 3-0 in NBA Cup play to maintain control of East Group C. The Wizards dropped to 2-2 in the NBA Cup.

Tatum led the effort with 41 points, 8 assists and 6 rebounds. He shot 6 of 15 from 3, but made all of them before halftime as cold second-half 3-point shooting helped the Wizards mount their rally.

Are Celtics shooting 3s that they don't need?

The Celtics were red-hot in the first half while shooting 15 of 26 (57.7%) from long distance. They shot 7 of 25 (28%) after halftime and needed three of those in the final minutes after the Wizards cut their deficit to five points.

Ultimately, their 43.1% success rate from 3 was a cornerstone of their win, but questions will surely surface about the wisdom of continuing to hoist up 3s after building a 31-point lead.

Paul George had no such struggles with a 28-point, 9-assist effort in which he shot 6 of 9 from 3. Anthony Davis led the Wizards with 33 points, 13 rebounds, 2 blocks and 1 steal.

Mavericks roll Nuggets to take control of group

In a matchup of a former NBA champion and four-time MVP against a lineup featuring a rising NBA start, youth prevailed in Denver.

Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks rolled a listless Nuggets team in Denver to the tune of a a 120-101 win.

The Mavericks limited the Nuggets to 17 first-quarter points, then closed the second quarter with a 15-0 run to take a 58-39 lead into the break.

The Nuggets answered with a 38-point third quarter and cut it as close as 80-77. But the Mavericks answered the run and closed the game strong to silence Ball Arena down the stretch with an overwhelming win.

Flagg led seven Mavericks players in double figures with 24 points, a career-high 12 assists and 6 rebounds.

Jamal Murray countered with 20 points and 3 rebounds on a 6-of-17 shooting effort. Nikola Jokić had a relatively quiet scoring night with 18 points, 11 rebounds, 5 assists and 5 turnovers.

With the win, the Mavericks (10-7) improved to 3-0 in Cup play to take control of West Group A. The Nuggets (10-5) dropped to 2-1 in the NBA Cup to fall behind the Mavs.

Pistons roll after concerning late scratch of Cade Cunningham

The Detroit Pistons secured an NBA Cup win over the Orlando Magic, but it was overshadowed by concern for Cade Cunningham, who was a late scratch due to a lingering knee injury .

The Pistons played without their All-NBA guard and cruised to a 104-86 win to hand the Magic their first loss in NBA Cup play. The Pistons (11-6) are now 2-1 in Cup play, while the Magic (7-10) drop to 3-1. The loss blocked the Magic from from a chance to clinch East Group A.

Cunningham was listed as probable prior to the game due to lingering knee soreness. But he was a late scratch before an NBA Cup game, raising concern that his injury is one that could further linger.

Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff declined to offer details on Cunningham's condition in his pregame news conference. He also didn't say much to tamp down concern.

"He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Bickerstaff said . "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got. But he's fighting through a lot."

Cunningham had previously missed one game this season, last Wednesday's 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans . He struggled in his previous outing with a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks.

Detroit struggled to get its offense going early without Cunningham as the Magic jumped out to a 22-16 first-quarter lead on their home court. But the Pistons seized control with a 32-14 advantage in the second quarter and kept the Magic at bay from there.

Isaiah Joe took Cunningham's place in the starting lineup and finished the game with a team-high 21 points alongside 4 rebounds and 1 steal. Daniss Jenkins was the primary playmaker in Cunningham's absence with 15 points and 10 assists. Desmond Bane led the Magic with 21 points and 5 assists.

George is in the midst of a career renaissance in his first season with the Celtics.

Wizards guard Kyshawn George learned the hard way Tuesday night. With the Celtics up big in the second half, Paul sized up Kyshawn in isolation.

He gained some separation with an arm extension on the perimeter, then crossed Kyshawn over as he drove to his right. Kyshawn did not stay with him.

Instead, Kyshawn fell on his backside onto the court and into the legs of his teammate, Anthony Davis.

Paul picked up his dribble and waited a beat while shooting a glance at Kyshawn — just to make sure Kyshawn was watching. Only then did Paul pull up for a jumper from just inside the 3-point arc that sank through the net to extend Boston's lead to 90-65 en route to its 15-point win.

Note: * denotes teams that have been eliminated from knockout-round contention.

articles.body: El Real Madrid y el Žalgiris Kaunas se enfrentan hoy, miércoles 25 de noviembre, en un nuevo partido de la fase regular de la Euroliga. El equipo madridista regresa a casa después de una semana complicada en Europa, en la que perdió sus dos partidos a domicilio frente al Besiktas y el Olympiacos. Esos resultados dejaron al conjunto blanco en la novena posición, dentro de la zona de play-in. El Real Madrid necesita recuperar sensaciones y frenar su mala dinámica ante un Žalgiris que llegaba a esta jornada situado inmediatamente por delante de los blancos en la clasificación. El conjunto lituano ya ha demostrado esta temporada que puede competir contra los principales aspirantes. En sus primeros encuentros derrotó al Estrella Roja y al Barcelona, aunque también perdió ante el Olympiacos, el París Basketball y el Fenerbahçe. El partido entre el Real Madrid y el Žalgiris Kaunas se disputa hoy, miércoles 25 de noviembre, a las 20:45 horas, según el horario peninsular español. El Real Madrid - Žalgiris se podrá ver en directo por televisión en España a través de Movistar Plus+. Además, todo lo que ocurra antes, durante y después del encuentro podrá seguirse en MARCA.com, con la previa, la narración en directo, las estadísticas, la crónica y las declaraciones de los protagonistas.

articles.title: La selección, a tomar Montenegro, el pequeño país de los gigantes
articles.standfirst: Segundo en el mundo por estatura media (1,83), la extraordinaria complexión física de sus hombres, por genética, dieta y geografía, le ayuda a brillar en el deporte
articles.summary: Montenegro, segundo en el mundo por estatura media (1,83),
articles.body: La selección de Chus Mateo viaja en las próximas horas a Podgorica, la capital oficial de Montenegro. Este jueves (19.00 h., TDP y Vamos) puede dar una apreciable zancada hacia el Mundial ahora que están a punto de ‘cerrarse’ (acabar) las Ventanas de Clasificación para Qatar 2027. El triunfo, que se considera casi imprescindible ante el colista del grupo I, unido a una hipotética victoria en Santiago de Compostela el domingo ante Grecia y otros resultados, pueden clasificar matemáticamente a la selección para el Campeonato del Mundo. España, después de dos derrotas consecutivas (Portugal y Grecia), quiere tomar el pequeño país de los gigantes. Montenegro es el segundo estado soberano del mundo con la media de estatura más alta: 183,8. Con 20 años de trayectoria como país independiente, la última república en abandonar lo que un día fue Yugoslavia tras transitar algunos años junto a Serbia, y algo más de 600.000 habitantes (menos que Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Zaragoza y Sevilla), 169 en el ranking mundial de población, a los ciudadanos de Montenegro le impulsan hacia las alturas la predisposición genética, la dieta y la localización geográfica. “Mar, montaña y la comida”, decía Radoncic, en una charla reciente con MARCA. La convocatoria de 19 jugadores de Mitrovic para recibir este jueves a España en el Moraça Sports Center (6.000 espectadores) tiene una estatura media de 2 metros, algo superior a la de España (1,98). Quizá tenga más mérito la talla del equipo de Mateo porque España es el país 56 del planeta en tamaño medio, con 1,76 en los hombres. El milagro de Montenegro, sólo por detrás de Países Bajos (1,84, de media masculina) en el escalafón, obedece a razones ancestrales que tiene que ver con los moradores de los Balcanes occidentales, cuyo perfil genético se remonta a los cazadores de caza mayor del Paleolítico Superior, hace 10.000 años, tirando por lo bajo. La orografía de los Alpes Dináricos ayudó a mantener relativamente aisladas a estas comunidades de gran complexión física. Después, la alimentación hizo el resto. Los lácteos, quesos locales y carnes, es decir, calcio y proteínas, forman parte de la dieta montenegrina. Si somos lo que comemos, competimos de acuerdo a nuestro talento y potencial físico. Montenegro tiene como deporte nacional al waterpolo. En la piscina logró su primer gran éxito como país con el título en el Europeo de 2008 y la Liga Mundial de 2009. Forma parte de la élite europea. El balonmano femenino dio la primera y única medalla olímpica para el país (plata en Londres 2012) y en baloncesto, sin haberse asomado todavía a unos Juegos Olímpicos, la selección balcánica alcanzó su cenit en el Mundial de 2023 con un undécimo puesto en un torneo donde alcanzó la segunda fase, logró una victoria histórica ante Grecia y compitió bien ante el Dream Team (73-85). De aquella selección, sólo sobreviven en la convocatoria actual seis jugadores: I. Drobnjak, Radoncic, Ilic, Simonovic, Slavkovic y Popovic. Montenegro está en un proceso de renovación. Materia prima no le falta. Dusko Ivanovic, montenegrino ilustre y autoridad en el baloncesto europeo, lo definía así en una entrevista en MARCA. “Lo que consigamos en el deporte se podría explicar a través de una predisposición física. Hay gente muy alta, con talento y que es competitiva desde el colegio”. Así es el país de los gigantes que mide a España.
