articles.title: Mark Pope provides injury update on Kentucky big man Malachi Moreno
articles.summary: Mark Pope said Malachi Moreno is responding well, after being in concussion protocol.
articles.body:
For Kentucky Basketball , it feels like when it rains, it pours, and the struggles continue to pile up for the Wildcats.

Kentucky has struggled against weaker opponents; along with that, it has suffered blowout losses against some of the better teams on its schedule. Now, the Wildcats could be without one of their most important players as they look to get the season back on track.

On Sunday, Matt Jones of Kentucky Sports Radio reported that sophomore center Malachi Moreno had entered concussion protocol after an Indiana player dove on him during Kentucky's loss to the Hoosiers. Moreno hit his head on the floor during the play and was unlikely to play in Friday's matchup against Wichita State.

Although Moreno remained in the game against Indiana, head coach Mark Pope provided an update on the sophomore big man during his radio show on Tuesday, explaining that Moreno began experiencing concussion symptoms on Saturday.

"He's doing good," Pope said on his radio show. "He kind of got a whole 270 pounds landed on his head, and kind of started after the game, and then especially, really the next day, started showing some symptoms.

"So we put him in concussion protocol, and he's responded really, really well, and so we're hopeful that he'll be back sooner rather than later because he's playing so well."

For Kentucky, losing Moreno for multiple games would be a significant setback, especially considering how productive he has been this season.

The sophomore center is averaging 13.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.8 blocks, and 1.2 steals in 27.8 minutes per game.

Wildcats fans are hopeful Moreno will be available for Friday's game against Wichita State, but his long-term health remains the priority as the season continues.

"He's put up huge numbers, and he's just playing at such a high level," Pope continued. "It's really important for us to get him back. We can't wait till we get him back, and he'll continue on with the terrific season."

With Moreno's status still uncertain, Kentucky will need its other frontcourt players to step up if the sophomore center is unable to return against Wichita State.

articles.title: Why Duke basketball is wearing 'Blueprint' jerseys for Prime Video games
articles.summary: Duke basketball will debut its new "Blueprint" uniforms against UConn and in all of its games on Prime Video this season. Here's why.
articles.body:
Duke basketball will debut new uniforms for its Amazon Prime games this season, beginning with Wednesday's matchup against UConn.

Known as the "Blueprint" uniforms, the jerseys are designed to honor Black history at Duke and Julian Abele and Claudius Claiborne.

Abele was an architect who helped design Duke University, including the Chapel, the Allen Building and Cameron Indoor Stadium. Claiborne was the first black student athlete at Duke, averaging 4.1 points, 1.9 rebounds and 0.9 assists across three seasons with the Blue Devils between 1966-1969.

The predominantly blue uniforms feature a black stripe down each side and include several tributes to Abele and Claiborne. Design elements include a blueprint of Cameron Indoor Stadium on the waistband, an arched "Duke" wordmark inspired by the uniforms worn during Claiborne's era and shadowed numbers that reference the behind-the-scenes contributions Abele made to the university's architecture. The side panels also feature architectural details inspired by Abele's designs.

Duke first unveiled the unfirosmon on Nov. 20 at a Community Event with Durham Public Schools Students.

The Blue Devils will tip off against the Huskies at 4 p.m. PT on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Duke's other games that will be on Prime Video this season include Texas Tech (Dec. 21) and Gonzaga (Feb. 20).

articles.title: UConn women's basketball facing hard truths as losses mount
articles.summary: Geno Auriemma questions UConn women's basketball's maturity and identity after a third loss exposed ongoing issues against top teams.
articles.body:
UNCASVILLE — Geno Auriemma sat at the podium looking as if the game followed him into the room.

The glasses came off. He rubbed his eyes. The collar of his white dress shirt hung open.

His answers arrived slowly, each one preceded by a pause that felt longer than the last. He searched for explanations, then searched again.

And with every question about UConn's 65-56 loss to South Carolina, another layer of frustration seemed to settle on his shoulders.

By the time Auriemma finished unpacking UConn's third loss of the season, he wasn't explaining why the Huskies missed shots or why the gameplan had run its course in the second half.

He had been confronting a reality that had been difficult to ignore.

"I'm having a really hard time coaching this team. I gotta figure it out, but it'd be nice if I could get some help," Auriemma said.

Three losses into a season that had national championship expectations written all over it, Auriemma is still waiting for his team to become what the Huskies have historically been.

The latest defeat, played less than an hour from campus in front of a heavily pro-UConn crowd, dropped the Huskies to 0-3 against elite opponents this season and exposed many of the same issues that surfaced in losses to Michigan and Louisville.

UConn actually won three of the four quarters against South Carolina but buried itself in a disastrous second period, getting outscored 27-6 in the decisive stretch.

Auriemma called that quarter the game. But afterward, his focus widened beyond one 10-minute collapse. His comments painted the picture of a coach growing increasingly exasperated with a group that has shown flashes of championship-level basketball without the consistency, toughness and poise required to sustain it against the nation's best teams.

"We're really immature," Auriemma said. "To play as hard as we did, and to compete as hard as we did today, and to hurt ourselves in so many ways. It's just disappointing. It really is. And obviously as a coaching staff, we're shaking our heads trying to figure out what new strategies we can come up with."

While the losses have piled up, the frustration for Auriemma has come in the fashion in which the Huskies have been defeated.

In all three games, UConn has played well defensively only for their offense to fail. Reigning national player of the year Sarah Strong has been consistently good, and freshman Jovana Popovic has shown she can be a solid No. 2.

But after those two, the scoring drops off significantly.

Sophomore Blanca Quiñonez had All-American expectations put on her by Auriemma early on but has not played to that expectation. In UConn's three losses, Quiñonez — who has missed all the offseason recovering from shoulder surgery — has averaged 4.3 points per game while shooting just over 20% from the field.

"We get a Blanca that fills the stat sheet against Iowa or against Seton Hall, and then we get the blocker that completely disappears in other games," Auriemma said. "You can chalk some of that up to I haven't played, but it's not all of it. It's just a having to be more disciplined and having to be more intentional."

Seniors Ashlynn Shade and KK Arnold haven't been productive on the offensive end. The center position has been platooned between veteran Jana El Afy and freshman Olivia Vukosa. The bench hasn't seen a spark all season despite having returning players such as Allie Ziebell and Morgan Cheli.

But the problem lies deeper than a few missed shots and a couple of turnovers.

Auriemma expressed frustration that his message isn't being heard. That when he says something in the huddle or in practice or in the locker room, it doesn't resonate.

Strong, the unquestioned leader of the Huskies, couldn't agree more.

"I just don't think we listen to him all the time, and that we don't trust him, and we need to. I mean, that's obviously on us, and we just have to change."

Now, with the Huskies sitting at 3-3, Auriemma is questioning whether the expectations were too much.

"Maybe I did this team a disservice," Auriemma said. "Maybe they're just not mentally ready for something like this. Maybe it's just too much for them.

"Maybe I overstated what kind of team we had mentally, and what I thought would be a great thing for them to experience. Maybe not so much."

The road will only get tougher from here. UConn still has ranked matchups with Duke, Maryland, Notre Dame and LSU on the schedule.

The Huskies are down two points guards as Arnold and Kayleigh Heckel were out vs South Carolina with injuries. Shooting guard Marine Dursus hasn't played since the season opener, dealing with a nagging foot injury that has kept her out of the lineup.

But still, Auriemma expects more from a program that is expected to be one of the nation's best.

"It's just so out of character for anybody that's been watching UConn play for 30-some years," Auriemma said. "I don't even recognize it. I don't recognize it."

articles.title: Battle 4 Atlantis 2026: Bracket, teams, schedule for college basketball tournament
articles.summary: The 2026 Battle 4 Atlantis will take place this week in the Bahamas, featuring two brackets. Here's what to know on the event, including game schedule and mo...
articles.body:
Feast Week returns to the Caribbean for one of college basketball's more well-known early-season multi-team events in the Battle 4 Atlantis.

And this year's multi-team event comes with a new twist, one that can likely be pointed to the continuous impact of the Players Era Festival in Las Vegas.

In its 15th iteration, the Battle 4 Atlantis will break into two separate four-team brackets that will see four teams — all of which are Power 5 opponents and the "big ticket" programs in the Bahamas this week — compete in a two-game event with tip-off times and matchups already predetermined before they boarded a charter plane.

The headliner of this year's Battle 4 Atlantis is Virginia, which once again was ranked in the top five of the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll. The Cavaliers, who have broken off from their accustomed style of play known under former head coach Tony Bennett in current head coach Ryan Odom, have a top-10 offense and a top-30 defense on KenPom. Thijs De Ridder has been on a tear to begin the season, finishing with 20 points in two of his last three games, and double digit figures in all seven of the Cavaliers' wins.

Marquette heads to the Bahamas looking to find its identity and bounce back from falling short in early tests against Michigan and Missouri, the latter of which the Golden Eagles saw an 11-point lead with seven minutes to go in the second half go away. The Golden Eagles will hope for Nigel James Jr. to heat up on the scoring end as well in their two games in the Bahamas, starting with Virginia on Wednesday.

There's also Memphis, Texas A&M and Xavier competing in the Bahamas this week, three teams that are looking to make the expanded 76-team NCAA tournament, with the Aggies and Mustkeeers shooting for at-large bids out of the SEC and Big East.

Here's everything you need to know about the 2026 Battle 4 Atlantis tournament, including who is in the bracket, game schedule, TV schedule and streaming information and more:

The men's Battle 4 Atlantis will start on Wednesday, Nov. 25 and run through Friday, Nov. 27 in The Bahamas. The Battle 4 Atlantis will not have any games on Thanksgiving this season, with the championship game set to take place on Friday with a tip-off time yet to be announced.

You guessed it, Atlantis in The Bahamas. But to be specific, Battle 4 Atlantis will once again take place inside the Imperial Arena at Atlantis Paradise Island in The Bahamas.

This year's Battle 4 Atlantis will still feature eight teams, but the event is introducing a new format. Rather than a traditional eight-team bracket, the field will be split into two separate four-team pods that will operate as independent tournaments.

Half of the field for the Battle 4 Atlantis is included in the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll, either ranked or receiving votes. Virginia, which was picked second behind Duke to win the ACC, headlines the pool of teams.

The two pods will be known as the "Championship Bracket" and the "Signature Series." Here's a breakdown of which team is in which bracket and pod:

articles.body:
In just a few days, the NCAA selection committee will unveil the official 64-team NCAA volleyball tournament bracket, signaling the official start of the Road to San Antonio.

Until then, let the bracketology continue in women's volleyball.

Both the Big Ten and SEC conference tournaments have generated significant discussion over the last week about how their respective tournaments have played out. First up, the SEC, where projected 1-seed Florida was upset in the quarterfinals by 9-seed Georgia in four sets. The Bulldogs then knocked off 5-seed Tennessee in a five-set thriller in the semifinals, the same night, 2-seed Kentucky swept 3-seed Vanderbilt to hand the Commodores their first loss in a month.

Because of the results in the SEC tournament, specifically Florida being upset, it has presented the opportunity for the Big Ten to steal the final 1-seed depending on who finishes as the likely runner-up to Nebraska in Fishers, Indiana. But for now, the Gators remain on the 1-seed line, but not with much room for separation. Michigan State picked up a win over Minnesota in the Big Ten tournament — and nearly beat Wisconsin — to move off the bubble in this latest bracket prediction.

articles.title: How Dawn Staley said Ashlyn Watkins disrupted Sarah Strong in South Carolina win vs UConn
articles.summary: South Carolina women's basketball forward Ashlyn Watkins' got her second start of the season with Joyce Edwards out vs. UConn.
articles.body:
UNCASVILLE, CT – It wasn't until about two hours before No. 1 South Carolina women's basketball tipped off against UConn that the Gamecocks learned star forward Joyce Edwards would not be able to play due to being sick.

According to coach Dawn Staley , Edwards missed shootaround earlier in the day to rest in hopes of feeling good enough to play but the made the call around 6 p.m. ET, that she didn't feel well enough.

In Edwards' absence, Ashlyn Watkins made her second start of the season for the Gamecocks (7-0) in their 65-56 win over No. 8 UConn at Mohegan Sun Arena on Nov. 24, playing a career-high 33 minutes.

"Yeah we had Joyce out, so folks had to step up, and I think that a lot of the girls stepped up, including Ash," guard Tessa Johnson said. "Ash was dominant out there, and yeah, she was ready."

South Carolina women's basketball vs UConn, Chloe Kitts, Sarah Strong see top photos

Watkins finished with seven points, eight rebounds, three blocks and four steals. Her contributions on the defensive end were crucial in helping the Gamecocks hold the Huskies to 26.6% shooting from the floor.

Watkins' defensive assignment for most of the night was star UConn forward Sarah Strong, who finished with 22 points but was 6-for-17 shooting.

"Don't let her catch it, really," Watkins said of defending Strong. "Just do your work early, and don't let her catch the ball that way she doesn't get in her rhythm, her rhythm of shots, rhythm of midranges. But she's a great player. She's going to get off regardless, but it's how she gets off. She's got to make harder shots, and that's what we made her do."

Staley called Watkins' performance "incredible" and credited Watkins' disruption of Strong's flow for making it easier for the Gamecocks' defense to shut down the Huskies offense, which runs primarily through Strong.

The performance was especially impactful, given it was only Watkins' seventh game back after missing the entire 2025-26 season and part of the 2024-25 season due to an ACL tear she suffered against Mississippi State on Jan. 5, 2025.

Watkins also made the decision to step away from the team before the 2025-26 season to "focus on myself, my community, my faith, and my family so that I can grow as an individual and attempt to master this journey of life," according to a statement she released on social media in July 2025.

Staley acknowledged that even while Watkins, and frontcourt mate Chloe Kitts, who also missed last season with a torn ACL, reacclimate to playing basketball, their presence on the court still positively influences the Gamecocks' play.

"They really understand who we are, how we need to play, and then they execute that," Staley said. "It may not always be pretty because … the two of them have not played basketball for a long stretch prior to our season, so they're still working out the kinks. They're still trying to find their footing, but what they continue to do is defend and rebound, and then the offense will come."

Tia Reid covers Jackson State sports for the Clarion Ledger . Email her at treid@usatodayco.com and follow her on X @tiareid65 .

articles.title: Who will be 'College GameDay' guest picker for Wake Forest-Duke? Potential choices
articles.summary: Who will be the "College GameDay" guest picker for Wake Forest-Duke? Here are some options.
articles.body:
ESPN's "College GameDay" is heading to Wake Forest for essentially the first time on Saturday, Nov. 28.

"GameDay" first went live from Winston-Salem, North Carolina, in 2020, although the pregame show was without fans in 2020. Now, Demon Deacons fans can enjoy the show and all its glory in-person amid an historic season.

Wake Forest can finish its regular season with an 11-1 record if it takes down Duke at home in Week 13, although it has already clinched a rematch against Miami in the ACC championship game.

Wake Forest has plenty of options to be the celebrity guest picker for "College GameDay." Who will the show choose? Here are a few options:

Wake Forest legend Chris Paul was the celebrity guest picker on "College GameDay" in 2020, but why not go with him again? Paul would be popular among the fans, and the guest picker should likely be one of the school's top representatives for an historic moment.

The future Basketball Hall of Famer is one of the greatest guards in NBA history, with 11 All-NBA selections before retiring midway through the 2025-26 season. Paul was drafted No. 4 overall in the 2005 NBA Draft out of Wake Forest and his No. 3 jersey is retired by the basketball program.

Another Wake Forest legend, Tim Duncan doesn't have the brightest personality but he's one of the greatest NBA players ever. It'd be hard to turn down.

The No. 1 overall pick of the 1997 NBA Draft out of Wake Forest won five NBA championships and two MVPS. He also won the 1997 Wooden Award, but Wake Forest lost in the second round of the NCAA tournament.

Paul and Duncan would be home-run guests for "GameDay."

Sam Hartman transferred to Notre Dame for his final season, but the former four-year starting quarterback at Wake Forest is one of the football program's best passers ever.

Hartman is also in the news of late, too, as he was named the next focus of ABC's "The Bachelor," which is also owned by Disney like "College GameDay."

Hartman is on the Washington Commanders ' practice squad, which could impact his availability for "GameDay."

One of the best young sluggers in MLB, Nick Kurtz was selected No. 4 overall in the 2024 MLB Draft out of Wake Forest before making his debut less than a year later, hitting 36 home runs in 2025.

Kurtz, who only played 99 games in 2026, still slugged 21 home runs and had an .879 OPS. Suffice to say, he's already one of the best hitters in the world.

Kurtz was a first-team All-American in 2023, helping lead Wake Forest to the College World Series, where it fell to eventual national champion LSU in the semifinals.

PGA Tour golfer Will Zalatoris has dealt with a myriad of injuries that have impacted his availability the last few seasons, but only a few years ago he was one of the most-promising young golfers on the tour.

Zalatoris played golf at Wake Forest from 2014-17 before turning pro, setting the school's scoring average record of 70.44. Zalatoris finished second in the Masters Tournament, PGA Championship and U.S. Open from 2021-22, with his highest Official World Golf Ranking reaching No. 7 in 2022.

articles.title: Five takeaways from Florida State home win over UNC Asheville
articles.summary: Florida State improved to 6-1 with a dominant victory over UNC Asheville, showcasing its physicality while facing a key injury concern.
articles.body:
Florida State continued its strong start to the 2026-27 season Tuesday night, defeating UNC Asheville 97-61 at the Donald L. Tucker Center to improve to 6-1 and extend its winning streak to four games.

The victory also featured a reunion for guard Kam Taylor, an injury concern involving Shon Abaev and another glimpse of what makes this Florida State team different from last year's squad.

Here are five instant takeaways from the Seminoles' latest home victory.

1. Florida State's biggest advantage isn't talent. It's physicality.

Opponents have increasingly discovered that keeping pace with Florida State for the opening 10 minutes is considerably easier than matching the Seminoles' intensity for an entire game.

Florida State's combination of size, athleticism and physical defense eventually wore down the Bulldogs, allowing the Seminoles to impose their style of basketball as the game progressed.

This has become a defining characteristic of Luke Loucks' squad. Rather than depending on extended stretches of hot shooting, Florida State can generate advantages through defensive pressure, rebounding, and attacking the paint.

Entering Tuesday, the Seminoles ranked among the nation's top 10 teams in rebounding margin, averaging nearly 44 rebounds per game. That physical advantage should become increasingly important as Florida State prepares for the considerably tougher competition awaiting it in ACC play.

2. Kam Taylor's reunion offers another glimpse of his potential

Tuesday's matchup carried additional significance for Kam Taylor, who faced his former program for the first time since transferring to Florida State. Taylor finished his reunion with 11 points, three rebounds and four assists, shooting just 3-of-7 from the field and converting all four of his free-throw attempts.

The 6-foot-7 guard is still adjusting to his role within Loucks' system, but his athleticism and ability to create scoring opportunities could eventually make him one of Florida State's most dangerous offensive weapons.

3. Loucks' demanding practices appear to be sending a message

Loucks hasn't been particularly satisfied with his team's intensity despite its recent success.

Following Florida State's previous three games, the second-year head coach expressed concerns about his players' energy and commitment to maintaining their defensive standards throughout an entire contest.

Loucks responded by putting the Seminoles through an exceptionally physical and demanding practice ahead of Tuesday's matchup. The message was straightforward: Winning games doesn't excuse inconsistent effort.

4. Free throws have completely changed Florida State's offensive identity

One of the most surprising developments through Florida State's opening seven games has been its dependence on getting to the free-throw line.

Entering Tuesday, the Seminoles had made 168 free throws while scoring 532 total points, meaning 31.6% of their offense had come from the charity stripe. Florida State was also shooting 81.6% from the line and averaging 28 made free throws per game, leading the nation in the latter category.

Those numbers reflect a significant shift in offensive philosophy.

By attacking the basket, drawing fouls and controlling the interior, Florida State has developed a more dependable foundation offensively. If the Seminoles can eventually combine that physicality with consistent perimeter shooting, they'll become a considerably more difficult matchup.

5. Shon Abaev's injury adds uncertainty as FSU searches for its shooting touch

Florida State received a concerning development during the first half when sophomore forward Shon Abaev exited the game with an apparent injury.

Abaev had been perfect from the field before departing, finishing with seven points, three rebounds and three assists in 10 minutes, shooting 3-of-3 overall and making his only three-point attempt.

His availability will be worth monitoring, as Abaev has been one of Florida State's most important perimeter scoring threats, averaging 14.2 points per game entering Tuesday.

articles.title: NBA power rankings: How far will slumping Thunder, Celtics fall?
articles.summary: For the first time since April 2023, the Oklahoma City Thunder have plunged to 10th place in the Western Conference standings.
articles.body:
As the NBA calendar churns on, Thanksgiving will give fans the chance to catch their breath — and, perhaps, catch some football.

No games will be played Thursday, Nov. 26, though NBA Cup action is starting to ramp up.

Another thing ramping up are the stakes, as certain contenders are facing adversity and losing skids. Chief among them are the Oklahoma City Thunder, who have been besieged by injuries and lost six of their last eight. In the East, it's the Boston Celtics who tumbled on a four-game losing streak, though they snapped it Tuesday, Nov. 24 against the Wizards. How far will both those teams fall?

Here are the Week 5 USA TODAY Sports NBA power rankings:

See the coolest sneakers of the NBA season

Movement from previous rankings in parentheses

Tyler Herro has embraced efficiency and has been on a scoring flash. Milwaukee's first win of November (against the Raptors) was a nice boost.

With all their injuries, they've had six different players lead the team in scoring over their last six games. That said, points are still too tough to come by.

A gritty win against the Celtics in which the Kings held Boston to just 13 points in the third quarter was a glimpse of what this roster can do when playing well. The problem? That doesn't happen anywhere near enough.

The offense has moments when it struggles to make baskets, but no team allows more points per 100 possessions than Brooklyn does, a staggering 120.3.

The Clippers rank second in the NBA in 3-point percentage (38.1%) but are middle of the pack in attempts (37.8 per game; tied for 15th).

Losers of 11 of their last 12, the Hornets have serious offensive issues and rank last in scoring, averaging just 100.6 points per game.

New Orleans isn't much better and has lost 10 of 11. The Pels also rank dead last in 3-point attempts per game (30.3).

Scottie Barnes has been stellar, but this team simply won't compete as long as Kawhi Leonard is sidelined. Toronto has lost seven of eight.

The Bulls have been far better as of late, with wins over the last 10 days against three teams in the top 15 of this list: the Hawks, Timberwolves and Cavaliers.

In their last game, they beat the injured Thunder (Shai Gilgeous-Alexander did play, however). That was a positive, but the Pacers offense cannot afford to be without Tyrese Haliburton. The good news? He practiced with Indiana's G League squad.

Anthony Davis has been superb and has stayed healthy, but Washington's other offensive weapons haven't been as consistent. Still, three wins in their last four is solid for the Wizards.

Franz Wagner was keeping Orlando competitive, but it has become clear, as teams have started to scout the Magic, that they miss Paolo Banchero (ankle). Even when he returns, however, he'll need reps to figure out how he jells with Wagner in new coach Sean Sweeney's system.

Since Stephen Curry (oblique) went down , the offensive production simply hasn't been there to sustain competitive play. Golden State ranks last in points per game (94.5) over the last six games.

Even though he hasn't been out long, and even though his production has dipped this season, the Cavs have regressed on defense and miss the scoring of Evan Mobley (toe).

After a slow start in which the offense lagged, Phoenix has won eight of its last 10. The Suns are doing a nice job of sharing the ball and limiting turnovers.

The other night against the Heat, the Thunder dressed just nine players because of injury. Their 10th place standing in the West is the lowest they've been since April 9 … of 2023.

They let the Mavericks clamp them up to go on a 17-0 run Tuesday night to close out the first half and begin the second, leading to a 21-point deficit. Low effort on transition defense compounded everything.

This young team has had some solid wins this season. And, with his blend of scoring and play-making, Cooper Flagg is well on his way to his first (of many) All-Star appearances.

It's clear Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard are the offensive catalysts. But since Ja Morant (hamstring) went out, no player has emerged as a third option.

The Grizz have continued to be one of the top surprises this season, but their star rookie, No. 3 overall pick Cameron Boozer, missing a month may set them back a touch.

Very quietly, the Hawks have been building a terrific season. They're the only team to average more than 30 assists per game, they rank fourth in second-chance points per game (16.9) and they've been playing cohesive and collaborative team defense.

Live by the 3, die by it; during Boston's recent four-game losing streak, which it snapped Tuesday night against the Wizards, the Celtics shot just 28.3% from beyond the arc.

They own the NBA's longest winning streak (seven games), have incorporated more on-ball screening and pick-and-rolls and an encouraging sign was that the offense rolled against a very depleted Thunder squad while Giannis Antetokounmpo was out.

After a slow start, the defending champs have settled in. They're leading the league in rebound percentage (53.8%). Karl-Anthony Towns leads the NBA in rebounding (13.9 per game) and hasn't had a single game in which he didn't reach double figures in the stat.

One of the more positive signs for Detroit has been its defense, which ranks fourth in rating (108.3) and tied for second in blocks per game (5.8) — all without Jalen Duren.

Houston has dropped two of its last four, both against solid opponents, but the Rockets have embraced efficiency, ranking third in true shooting (59.9%) and effective field goal percentage (56.0%).

Ayo Dosunmu has been a revelation for the Timberwolves with Anthony Edwards (knee) out, and his steady scoring has kept the offense afloat.

With Autin Reaves (heel) out, things have been shakier lately, though just one loss in their last 12 shows this team has staying power. But L.A. could use a Reaves return.

Joel Embiid's illness has come at a tough time, as he had just started to find his offensive dominance, scoring 29.7 points over his last three.

Even without Dylan Harper (hip), the Spurs are thriving, and Victor Wembanyama is playing at an MVP level . San Antonio also leads the NBA in net rating (+12.3).
